Our study also constitutes an extension of

targets.authors: Cooper, A. C., Gimeno-Gascon, F. J., & Woo, C. Y.
targets.title: Initial human and financial capital as predictors of new venture performance.
targets.evidence_quote:
The present study attempts to avoid fragmentation
and contribute to cumulative knowledge by replicating – to the extent possible – the study
carried out by Cooper, Gimeno-Gascon & Woo (1994).
targets.outcome_quote:
On a conceptual level, our results
       confirm those obtained by Cooper et al. (1994) regarding how general human capital,
       management know-how and industry affect marginal survival probability, as well as
       concerning the effects of financial and general human capability on the likelihood of
       becoming a high performance venture. The results sometimes coincide also on a very detailed
       level, such as the differential effect of gender on marginal survival vs. its effect on high
       performance. Other parts of Cooper et al’s (1994) result could not be replicated.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly identify conceptual confirmations and other original results that could not be replicated. Their detailed comparison and discussion likewise present both agreements and differences. Measurement limitations qualify interpretation but do not replace this mixed verdict with a claim that the attempt cannot adjudicate.
